moat_against: Single-counterparty concentration: substantially all revenue is the management fee on one reciprocal Exchange's premiums — no diversification if the Exchange shrinks
Fee rate is capped at 25% and already there — zero pricing headroom; the Board can cut the rate, and growth must come entirely from Exchange premium volume
Concentrated regional footprint (Pennsylvania-weighted) and policies in force fell ~2% in H1 2026 with retention easing to 87.5% — the premium base is currently shrinking on a unit basis

Cost linkage to the Exchange's underwriting cycle: agent incentive compensation rises when the Exchange's combined ratio improves (H1 2026 commissions +8.1% vs management fee revenue +4.5%), squeezing the spread exactly when the Exchange does well
moat_for: Attorney-in-fact structure since 1925: subscribers appoint Indemnity under the subscriber's agreement — no contract bidding, effectively perpetual
Management fee held at the 25% contractual maximum (2024, 2025, and set again for 2026) — proven, durable pricing on the Exchange's premium base
ROIC proxy 23.9% / 20.1% / 22.6% / 27.0% / 31.3% / 28.7% for 2020-2025 (fundamentals.json) — well above cost of capital through the cycle; no debt on the balance sheet
Exclusive independent-agent network and top-ranked customer satisfaction (J.D. Power #1 among large auto insurers, third straight year in 2026) support 87.5% retention
moat_justification: Century-old attorney-in-fact lock-in on the Erie Insurance Exchange (since 1925) with the management fee held at the 25% contractual maximum, and ROIC proxy of 20-31% in every year 2020-2025 — but the fee rate is capped with no pricing headroom, and the entire revenue base is one counterparty in a concentrated regional footprint whose policies in force are now shrinking.
name: Erie Indemnity Company
one_liner: Durable fee franchise, moat 7/10 (attorney-in-fact since 1925, fee at the 25% cap, ROIC 20-31%) — but priced for the old growth: TTM base $10.57/share at $242.68 gives a 7.7% weighted IRR, Tier D; clears 15% only below $98.16 (weighted IV@15%).

sbc_override.ack_reason: Out-of-band by construction: the engine has no filed SBC value to band against (no SBC fact under any candidate tag in any period of companyfacts), so any value flags out-of-band. The $0 is not an estimate — it is the filing-proven figure: Note 11 states no new shares are issued for any plan and all open LTIP periods are cash-payable, and the direct-method cash-flow statement reconciles exactly with no SBC line in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025.
sbc_override.reason: DATA_GAP:sbc — SBC missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 under every tag the engine reads, because Erie has no equity-settled share-based compensation to subtract. Note 11: 'We do not issue new shares of common stock to satisfy plan awards' (ECP) / 'to settle stock awards' (LTIP) / 'to directors' (deferred stock plan) — every share-linked award is settled in cash or with Class A shares purchased on the open market (treasury/rabbi-trust shares), the open LTIP performance periods (2023-2025, 2024-2026, 2025-2027) are all payable in cash, and the costs are liability-accrued compensation already inside operating expenses. The cash-flow statement is direct-method (cash receipts minus cash paid, fully enumerated for FY2023-FY2025 with no SBC addback or non-cash compensation line), so the compensation cost already sits inside reported OCF — subtracting an SBC figure again would double-count it (same treatment as COKE/SQM/LTM in this sweep). The filing-proven equity-settled SBC figure for the gap years is $0.
sbc_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-23, accession 0001628280-26-010666), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (direct method, fully enumerated) and Note 11, Incentive and Deferred Compensation Plans. EDGAR companyfacts for CIK 922621 contains no ShareBasedCompensation / AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense fact in any period.

shares_override.ack_reason: Out-of-band by construction if the engine bands against the filed share facts: the only undimensioned diluted fact in companyfacts is the 2,542 Class B share count, not a company-wide denominator. The value is not an estimate — it is exactly the diluted weighted-average Class A count printed in the FY2025 10-K's statements of operations and EPS note, which under the if-converted method carries total net income ($559,335k / 52,305,424 = the reported $10.69 diluted EPS).
shares_override.reason: DATA_GAP:shares — diluted shares missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 in companyfacts because the filer tags share counts only by share class (the only undimensioned WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding fact in companyfacts is the 2,542-share Class B count). The filer's own FY2025 Class A diluted weighted-average count — computed under the if-converted method, i.e. including assumed conversion of the 2,542 Class B shares (2,400:1 = 6,100,800 Class A equivalents) and the dilutive effect of stock-based awards (15,600 shares) — fills the gap. The engine applies this single value to every missing period; the filer's own FY2024/FY2023 diluted counts (52,306,266 / 52,299,411) differ from it by less than 0.02%, so no year's OE/share is materially moved.
shares_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-23, accession 0001628280-26-010666), Consolidated Statements of Operations and Note 5, Earnings Per Share: weighted average shares outstanding — Diluted, Class A common stock 52,305,424 for FY2025 (52,306,266 FY2024; 52,299,411 FY2023); Class A diluted EPS $10.69 on total net income $559,335 thousand under the if-converted method (52,305,424 x $10.69 = total net income, i.e. this denominator carries the whole company's earnings including the Class B allocation).
